Modulation of cellular signalling pathways and the anti-cancer actions of UC2288 in UM cells

Overview of the modulation of cellular signalling pathways and the anti-cancer actions of UC2288 in UM cells.UC2288 arrests the cell cycle in S phase and modulates CDK2, cyclin E1 and A2 protein expression, impairs metastasis and decreases EMT proteins (such as E-cadherin, vimentin, MMP2 and β-catenin), promotes ROS production and activates the AMPK/eIF2/ATF4 pathway that regulates ER stress
Download JPG
View figure at PMC Read paper at PMC

Publication

UC2288 decreases the viability and metastatic activity of human Uveal Melanoma cells via activating the AMPK/eIF2/ATF4 ER stress axis (2026) Janney Z Wang, et al. Eur J Pharmacol. 2026 Mar 28;1019(NA). Figure: F8.
